correctness.rationale: For n>=2, a prescribed r-set of pairwise disjoint cyclic adjacent chords has probability (2n-2r-1)!!/(2n-1)!!; there are M(n,r)=2n/(2n-r)*binom(2n-r,r) such sets. Removing them leaves the full crossing statistic exactly unchanged. Ordered selection yields E[(S_n)_r f(C_n)]=r! b(n,r) E[f(C_{n-r})], hence the bivariate generating polynomial for every complex u,v including r=n with C_0=0. r=1,2 and the independently established exact C_m moments yield Corr(S,C)=-sqrt(5/(n+3)). For fixed r, the classical crossing CLT for n-r and r!b(n,r)->1 give all mixed factorial Gaussian limits. Uniform boundedness of higher S moments yields UI, tightness and PGF uniqueness imply the independent Pois(1) x N(0,1) joint law and CLT conditional on S=0. An independent direct enumeration generated all pairings n=2..6 (3,15,105,945,10395), checked every r and full mixed crossing-count distributions, all matched. The enumerations are finite; the infinite proof is analytic.
